citation: AND-cross-composition (Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2014) + AND-distillation lower bound (Drucker, FOCS 2012 / SICOMP 2015)
note: Disjoint union of t planar 3-colouring instances is planar, has treewidth = max_i tw(x_i) ≤ poly(max input size), and is 3-colourable iff ALL components are. That is a valid AND-cross-composition from NP-hard planar 3-colouring, so no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. (Coloring param by treewidth is FPT via 3^tw·n DP.)

citation: Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Kernelization Lower Bounds Through Colors and IDs', ACM Trans. Algorithms 11(2):13 (2014); prelim. ICALP 2009
note: Connected Vertex Cover param by k is one of the flagship no-poly-kernel results proved there via composition (colors-and-IDs). FPT (2^k·n^{O(1)}).

citation: Hagerup, 'Kernels for Edge Dominating Set: Simpler or Smaller', MFCS 2012; cf. Xiao–Kloks–Poon 2013
note: Endpoints of an edge dominating set of size k form a vertex cover of size ≤2k, enabling a kernel with O(k^2) vertices/edges. Poly kernel.

citation: Estivill-Castro, Fellows, Langston, Rosamond, 'FPT is P-time Extremal Structure I' (2005) — 3.75k-vertex kernel; cf. Fellows et al. quadratic kernel
note: Max-Leaf (spanning tree with ≥k leaves) has a linear-vertex kernel (≤3.75k). Poly kernel.

citation: Reduction from Steiner Tree param by #terminals (no poly kernel: Dom–Lokshtanov–Saurabh, ACM TALG 2014 / ICALP 2009)
note: Setting each Steiner terminal's prize to +∞ (>> incident edge costs) makes it a proper potential terminal and forces its inclusion, so Steiner Tree with k terminals = PCStT with |T^+_p|=k. Parameter-preserving, hence no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. FPT in |T^+_p| by the potential-terminals branching.

citation: Bessy, Fomin, Gaspers, Paul, Perez, Saurabh, Thomassé, 'Kernels for feedback arc set in tournaments', JCSS 77 (2011) — (2+ε)k / linear kernel; earlier Dom–Guo–Hüffner–Niedermeier–Truß O(k^2)
note: FAST admits a linear-vertex kernel. Poly kernel (contrast general directed FAS, which is open).

citation: Betzler, Fellows, Guo, Niedermeier, Rosamond, 'Fixed-parameter algorithms for Kemeny rankings', TCS 410 (2009); refined partial kernel Betzler–Bredereck–Niedermeier, JAAMAS 2014
note: Score ≤k bounds total pairwise disagreement by k: ≤O(k) 'dirty' candidates (candidates linear in the score / avg KT-distance) and ≤k deviating votes (identical votes bundled with binary multiplicities). Problem kernel of size poly(k).

citation: Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Kernelization Lower Bounds Through Colors and IDs', ACM Trans. Algorithms 11(2):13 (2014); prelim. ICALP 2009
note: Capacitated Vertex Cover param by k proven to have no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (same colors-and-IDs composition paper). FPT.

parameterization: solution size k (d-Set Packing, set size ≤ d fixed)
citation: Sunflower (Erdős–Rado) kernelization, O(k^d) sets — Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015) ch.2; Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Zehavi, Kernelization (2019)
note: d-Set Packing has an O(k^d)-set sunflower kernel; poly for fixed d. (Color-coding gives the FPT algorithm; the kernel is via sunflowers.) Dell–Marx (SODA 2012): no O(k^{d-ε}) kernel, but poly kernel exists.

citation: Reduction from Steiner Tree param by #terminals (no poly kernel: Dom–Lokshtanov–Saurabh, ACM TALG 2014 / ICALP 2009)
note: A Steiner Tree instance with k terminals = Group Steiner Tree with k singleton groups (parameter-preserving), so no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. FPT in #groups (Dreyfus–Wagner-style DP).

citation: AND-cross-composition (disjoint union) + Drucker AND-distillation lower bound (FOCS 2012 / SICOMP 2015); framework Bodlaender–Downey–Fellows–Hermelin, JCSS 2009
note: Treedepth of a disjoint union = max of components' treedepths, so union has td ≤ k iff all components do — an AND-cross-composition from NP-hard Treedepth. No poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. Computable in FPT (2^{O(k^2)}·n / linear-FPT) time.

citation: van Bevern, Moser, Niedermeier, 'Kernelization Through Tidying', LATIN 2010 (O(k^2) kernel); CVD is a special case of 3-Hitting Set (hit all induced P3), giving an O(k^2)-vertex kernel
note: Cluster graphs = P3-free, so CVD = 3-Hitting Set on P3-triples → O(k^2)-vertex kernel (O(k^3) weighted). Poly kernel.

citation: Kim, Williams, 'Improved Parameterized Algorithms for Constraint Satisfaction', IPEC 2010 (arXiv:1008.0213) — O(k)-variable bikernels for Boolean CSPs of arity c above average
note: Each arc (u,v) is the arity-2 Boolean constraint x_u∧¬x_v, satisfied with prob 1/4 under a random assignment, so m/4 is exactly the average. 'Above m/4' = Boolean 2-CSP above average → O(k)-variable bikernel; with NP-completeness this yields a polynomial kernel (O(k^2) constraints).

citation: Sunflower-lemma kernel, O(k^d) sets — Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015) ch.2; Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Zehavi, Kernelization (2019); orig. Abu-Khzam 2010
note: The sunflower kernel gives ≤ d!·k^d sets (O(k^{d-1}) improvements known). Textbook poly kernel; Dell–Marx show no O(k^{d-ε}) kernel.

parameterization: number of distinct item sizes d
citation: No kernel or kernel-lower-bound result located for this parameter; even FPT-by-d is not established (Goemans–Rothvoß / Jansen–Klein give (log Δ)^{2^{2^d}}-type XP algorithms, which are not f(d)·poly)
note: Honest open: high-multiplicity/number-problem structure; the row's 'FPT in #distinct sizes' claim rests on XP/quasi-poly algorithms, not an FPT algorithm, so no poly kernel is known (kernel would imply FPT). Could not settle — no establishing R20 citation exists.

citation: Nemhauser–Trotter / crown 2k-vertex kernel (Chen–Kanj–Xia 2010); linear kernel on planar graphs, Alber–Fellows–Niedermeier, JACM 2004
note: Vertex Cover has a 2k-vertex kernel in general; planar keeps a linear kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Alber, Fellows, Niedermeier, 'Polynomial-time data reduction for dominating set', JACM 51(3):363–384 (2004) — first linear kernel for planar dominating set
note: Linear O(k)-vertex kernel via region decomposition (bidimensionality). Poly kernel.

citation: Four Colour Theorem (Appel–Haken 1977; Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas 1997) — trivial 4k kernel; cf. bidimensionality linear kernels (Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Thilikos)
note: Planar graphs have an independent set of size ≥ n/4, so if k ≤ n/4 answer YES, else n < 4k — a linear (4k-vertex) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: FPT: Chen, Liu, Lu, O'Sullivan, Razgon, JACM 55(5) (2008). Poly kernel is a well-known OPEN problem (as for Directed Feedback Vertex Set); noted open in Cygan et al. (2015)
note: Directed FAS/FVS is FPT but existence of a polynomial kernel is famously open — neither a poly kernel nor a no-poly lower bound is known.
